doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Own bands: swing concert, Brunswick, RCA
title: Autonomy clause in his RCA contract; the Billie Holiday Any Old Time dispute
summary: His contract gave total control over repertoire; Billie's Any Old Time was withheld because of her Brunswick contract, and Helen Forrest sang it.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: How did . . . It would be good to know about how the record company worked with you at the time. Did you . . . did they dictate to you what you recorded?
No. I had a contract that says no-one could dictate. The contract stated that I had total autonomy over what I recorded. They didn’t have to release it, but they had to pay

me the advance. I didn’t know that they didn’t have to release it, or I’d have insisted on that too, because they wouldn’t release the Billie Holiday record of Any Old Time. But then I found out much later why that was. The real reason was that she had signed contracts with Brunswick and kept on signing them while she was with my band. I don’t know. So weird. Anyway, Brunswick raised hell when they heard the Victor record of Any Old Time. It had to be withdrawn. So then I let Helen Forrest sing it. Later, of course, it’s all come out in the wash now, and Billie’s is the record that they hear now, because she become a piece of mythology today.
